name: Yifang Wang
statement: I shape and build products, from their purpose and business model to the details of how they work.

projects.name: Photolio
projects.summary: A physical home for digital memories. Product strategy, NFC interactions, and a publishing platform for stories people share.
projects.title: Giving shared memories a place in everyday life
projects.lead: Product strategy, design, and development for an NFC-connected platform that brings photographs, voices, and shared stories into physical keepsakes.
brief: Develop a memory product around the moments people already celebrate and share. Connect a physical gift with a digital space where friends and family can contribute their own photographs, recordings, and words—and where the recipient can return to the story.
response: Working with my co-founder, I helped shape Photolio around NFC-connected keepsakes, bringing the object, its content, and the experience of giving it into one product. I led product and interaction design, built the frontend, and worked across backend integration and deployment.

The platform brings media collection, shared editing, and playback into a connected experience. An NFC-enabled object provides access to the story; the digital space gives that story room for multiple voices and formats. My work extended into product selection and promotional design, connecting what we built with how people would encounter and understand it.
I later extended the platform into personal publishing, allowing people to arrange existing content into their own public spaces. My portfolio became the first use case for this new direction.

themes.heading: An object with a story inside
text: A photograph can sit on a shelf. A recording can preserve a voice. Photolio brings them together through an object someone can give, keep, and revisit. I designed the interactions around preparing the content, inviting contributions, and opening the finished collection.
themes.caption: Physical keepsakes connected to photographs, video, audio, and shared writing.

themes.heading: Designing for the way it reaches people
text: We explored graduation keepsakes, event commissions, and partnerships with florists and photography studios. Each setting placed different demands on the product and its presentation. Conversations with prospective partners also brought service credibility and content preservation into focus, informing clearer business information on the website and changes to backup arrangements.
themes.caption: Product selection and communication developed alongside the digital experience.

themes.heading: Built to keep. Free to take with you.
text: Trust is part of the product experience. Alongside the publishing interface, I worked on the website’s explanation of storage, backups, and content portability—making the service behind a keepsake easier to understand.
The product website presents cloud and local storage, encrypted transfer, and export arrangements through a series of simple illustrations.
themes.caption: A visible account of where memories live and how they can leave.

themes.heading: A clear path from choosing to publishing
text: The editor separates selecting content, previewing it, and adding it to a page. Reusable content blocks support different formats, while viewing and editing permissions remain distinct. I developed these interactions directly in code, carrying the design through responsive layouts, media reading, and the deployed web experience.
themes.caption: Select, preview, arrange, and publish.

details: Developed with my co-founder at Xiedao Renaissance
Product strategy, interaction design, frontend development, backend integration, deployment, promotional design
Vue 3, TypeScript, uni-app, Python, FastAPI, Tailscale, RAID, NFC, Umami

projects.name: MIAOZER
projects.summary: AI assistance built into the work of renovating a home. Product design and development across iOS, Android, and WeChat.
projects.title: Bringing AI into the work of renovating a home
projects.lead: Product design and cross-platform development connecting renovation advice with project plans, materials, and local service providers.
brief: Introduce AI capabilities into an existing renovation platform. Give homeowners a connected way to plan work, document progress, and find relevant products and professionals, while fitting the platform’s established mobile experiences and client delivery requirements.
response: Working with my co-founder on MIAOZER’s AI upgrade, I designed and developed interfaces across iOS, Android, and WeChat mini-programs. My work connected the assistant to renovation diaries and platform search, so a conversation could lead into a plan, a product page, or a service-provider profile.

I also built Python assistant workflows that bring project context and retrieved platform information into the conversation. Speech input and image-based material recognition provide additional ways to begin a task. Across these features, I focused on the relationship between what the assistant says and what the user can do next.
I developed the backend agent workflows; my co-founder developed the RAG-based intelligent search. I integrated the two into the cross-platform experience.
The completed engagement was accepted by the client.

themes.heading: Advice with somewhere to go
text: Product and provider recommendations appear as actionable cards built from platform records. The conversation provides context; the cards lead to the relevant information. I connected these elements across search, streamed responses, and conversation history, giving the assistant a practical role within the existing product.
themes.caption: From a question to a product or service-provider page.

themes.heading: A plan organized around the home
text: The renovation diary gives each project a structure of rooms and steps, with progress and media attached to the work they describe. I developed the interfaces and assistant integration around that structure, including the states that show when a plan is being generated, is ready, or needs another attempt.
themes.caption: Project, room, and task views bring the renovation into focus at different scales.

themes.heading: A connected experience across three platforms
text: I carried the interaction design into Swift, Kotlin, and uni-app implementations, aligning navigation, chat, diary behavior, and media input. Shared API contracts connected the clients to the same underlying workflows, while each implementation accounted for its platform’s behavior.
themes.caption: iOS, Android, and WeChat interfaces for the same renovation workflows.

details: Client project, undertaken with my co-founder
Interaction design, cross-platform frontend development, Python assistant workflows, API integration

projects.name: Xiedao Renaissance
projects.summary: A writing assistant shaped around the writer’s intent. Conversational design, training-data development, and specialized language-model experiments.
projects.title: Making room for the writer’s intent
projects.lead: Conversational design and language-model experimentation for a writing assistant that helps people develop an idea through dialogue.
brief: Develop an AI writing experience around the decisions that give a story its direction. Help writers articulate their ideas, explore a setting, and work through character motivations and narrative structure, with a specialized model suited to the venture’s computing resources.
response: I designed a conversational approach that begins with focused questions and builds on the writer’s answers. The interaction moves from an initial idea toward a more developed story, using each exchange to clarify choices about the world, its characters, and the events that connect them.

To support this direction, I built Python pipelines for collecting and organizing reference material, then preparing instruction and multi-turn conversation data. I experimented with Qwen fine-tuning through LLaMA-Factory and quantization using AWQ and GPTQ, bringing the interaction objective into the model-development process.

themes.heading: The next question shapes the story
text: The dialogue examples explore how an assistant can follow an idea across several levels: a character’s immediate goal, the rules of the setting, and the larger narrative. I used these examples to define the intended questioning behavior and guide training-data preparation.
themes.caption: A conversation structure for moving from an initial premise to a developed direction.

themes.heading: Giving reference material a useful structure
text: I scraped public-domain classics and open wikis, then built Python pipelines to classify and organize the material into Alpaca instruction records and ShareGPT conversations. I adjusted semantic-layer parameters while exploring style mimicry and worldbuilding depth.
themes.caption: Reference material, structured records, and multi-turn training examples.

themes.heading: Specialization within practical limits
text: I deployed Dockerized training environments on AutoDL GPU instances and used LLaMA-Factory to fine-tune Qwen, followed by AWQ and GPTQ quantization experiments. I served fine-tuned models with vLLM, Nginx frontend services and Cloudflare domain routing.
themes.caption: Applied model experiments supporting a defined product direction.

details: Early AI-writing work at Xiedao Renaissance
Conversational design, data pipelines, training-example development, fine-tuning and quantization experiments
Python, Qwen, LLaMA-Factory, Alpaca, ShareGPT, Docker, AutoDL, AWQ, GPTQ, vLLM, Nginx, FastAPI, Cloudflare

projects.name: Brookline Interactive Group
projects.summary: Community media in practice. Location shoots, live production, editing, and workflow automation during a summer internship.
projects.title: On site. On air.
projects.lead: Camera operation, live production, editing, and workflow automation at Brookline Interactive Group.
brief: Support the recurring work of making municipal meeting recordings available through the organization’s publishing system, alongside the demands of live media production.
response: During my media internship, I developed a Python and Selenium workflow to download, process, and upload meeting videos to Cablecast.tv. The automation connected repetitive publishing steps within an environment I also supported through camera operation, live production, and meeting displays.
projects.caption: A publishing workflow built around the needs of a working media organization.
details: 10+ on-location shoots, two edited video projects, live multi-camera production, Town Meeting voting displays, and workflow automation
Python, Selenium, FFmpeg, Broadcast Pix, Panasonic HC-X2, Cablecast.tv, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Motion Array

about: I’m Yifang Wang, a product designer and developer, Media Science senior at Boston University, and co-founder of Xiedao Renaissance, a MiraclePlus-backed venture.

I work across product direction, interaction design, and implementation. In a small team, that has meant helping decide what to build, developing the experience directly in code, and staying with it through deployment and customer feedback.

My background in media production and communication informs how I present products as well as how I build them. I’m interested in the relationship between an idea, the way people encounter it, and the systems that make it work.
credit: Built with Photolio’s personal-space platform, a product I co-developed.
